name: Denmark
description: Denmark consistently ranks among the world's happiest countries, offering expats a high quality of life, a robust social welfare system, and a progressive culture. It's a peaceful and safe environment that prioritizes work-life balance and environmental consciousness.
longdescription: Expat life in Denmark is characterized by a strong emphasis on well-being and a highly organized society. The country boasts a high standard of living, supported by an excellent public healthcare system and free education. Danish culture, while initially reserved, values equality, modesty, and privacy, with the concept of 'hygge' fostering a sense of coziness and contentment. Punctuality is important, and informal addressing is common. The economy is robust, and salaries generally match the high cost of living, especially for skilled workers in fields like IT and engineering. Denmark is a leader in environmental sustainability, with extensive cycling infrastructure and a commitment to renewable energy. Crime rates are very low, contributing to a strong sense of safety. However, the high cost of living, particularly in cities like Copenhagen, and the cold, long winters can be challenges for newcomers. Integration into Danish social circles may take time, as Danes tend to maintain long-standing friendships.

visas.name: Simplified work permit (Denmark)
visas.description: Simplified work permit scheme for highly paid positions or certified companies in Denmark.
benefits: High quality of life
Work-life balance
Strong welfare system
Family inclusion
Schengen access

visas.name: Denmark Student Residence Permit
visas.description: Denmark's student residence permit for non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled in a full-time study programme at a Danish university or higher education institution lasting more than 3 months.
benefits: Study in Denmark
Part-time work permitted (20hrs/week)
Post-study work permit option
High quality of life
Schengen Area travel

visas.name: Denmark Family Reunification Permit
visas.description: Denmark's family reunification permit allows spouses, registered partners, and minor children of Danish residents to join them in Denmark, subject to integration and attachment requirements.
benefits: Family unity in Denmark
Right to work
Path to permanent residency
Strong welfare system
Schengen Area travel

visas.name: Fast-Track Scheme
visas.description: The Fast-Track Scheme is a special business scheme administered by SIRI that allows certified Danish companies to quickly and flexibly recruit highly qualified employees, specialists, or managers from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. It offers a streamlined process for obtaining residence and work permits, allowing foreign employees to start working sooner and providing flexibility for work performed both in Denmark and abroad.
visas.target_applicant: Highly qualified employees, specialists, managers, or researchers from countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who have been offered employment by a SIRI-certified Danish company.
visas.renewal_conditions: If employed for a shorter period than 4 years, the permit will normally be valid for the employment period. To continue working after this, an extension must be applied for.
benefits: Faster application processing and possibility of a 'quick job start' allowing work to commence while the permit is being processed.
Flexibility to work alternately in Denmark and abroad without losing the permit.
Allows job content changes (e.g., promotion, change of workplace) within the same certified company without requiring a new work permit.
Often allows family members (spouse/children) to be granted a residence permit.
Entitlement to partly user-paid Danish lessons.
required_documents: Documentation of paid fee (receipt).
Copy of all pages of the applicant's passport (including empty pages, front and back cover).
Power of attorney from the applicant.
Employment contract or job offer, not more than 30 days old, detailing salary, terms of employment, and job description.
Documentation of educational background.
Documentation of authorisation, if the job requires a Danish authorisation.
Documentation of legal stay in Denmark, if applicable.
Documentation for any salary components not directly stated in the employment document, if relevant.
application_process_steps: Receive a job offer from a SIRI-certified Danish employer.
Your employer submits the online application for a residence and work permit on your behalf via the Fast-Track Scheme and pays the processing fee.
Create a case order ID.
Record biometric features (facial photo and fingerprints) at a Danish diplomatic mission or SIRI no later than 14 days after application submission.
SIRI processes the application and grants a residence and work permit if requirements are met.

visas.name: Pay Limit Scheme
visas.description: The Pay Limit Scheme is designed for non-EU/EEA nationals who have been offered a highly paid job in Denmark. It grants a residence and work permit, allowing the holder to live and work in the country, contributing to the Danish labor market.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are skilled professionals from outside the EU/EEA who have secured a job offer in Denmark with an annual salary meeting a specified high threshold, without requiring a specific educational background or professional field.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After four years of continuous legal residency in Denmark under the Pay Limit Scheme, individuals may apply for permanent residency, provided they meet specific requirements, including Danish language proficiency. After nine years of permanent residency, it is possible to apply for Danish citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the required annual salary (adjusted yearly) and employment conditions corresponding to Danish standards. Application for extension must be submitted before the current permit expires.
benefits: Allows work and residency in Denmark without requiring a specific educational background or job field.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency in Denmark.
Permits family reunification for spouses, partners, and children.
Offers relatively quick processing times compared to other immigration routes.
Allows changes in job content or promotions within the same company/university without needing a new work permit.
required_documents: Valid passport (copy of all pages, including empty ones and covers).
Signed employment contract or job offer (not more than 30 days old) detailing job title, responsibilities, salary, and terms of employment.
Documentation of education relevant to the job offered (diplomas, certificates).
Curriculum Vitae (CV) detailing work experience and skills.
Passport-sized photographs.
Completed application form (AR1).
Documentation of authorization, if the job requires a Danish authorization.
application_process_steps: Secure a job offer from a Danish employer that meets the minimum salary requirement.
The employer creates a case order ID for the application and completes their part of the application.
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are current and translated if necessary.
Create a user account on the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration (SIRI) online portal and pay the application fee.
Submit the application online through SIRI's official website or a Danish diplomatic mission/application center.
Await processing and decision from SIRI; be prepared to provide additional information if requested.

visas.name: Supplementary Pay Limit Scheme
visas.description: The Supplementary Pay Limit Scheme in Denmark is designed for non-EU/EEA nationals who have been offered a high-paying job in Denmark. It allows individuals to obtain a residence and work permit without requiring a specific educational background or a job within a particular professional field, provided certain salary and employment conditions are met.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals from third countries who have received a job offer in Denmark with an annual salary meeting the specified threshold, and whose position has been publicly advertised.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Supplementary Pay Limit Scheme can lead to permanent residency in Denmark. Typically, applicants must have lived in Denmark for a minimum of four years, maintained employment meeting the salary threshold, and demonstrated Danish language proficiency.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicant must continue to be employed in the same position and by the same employer, having worked and received salary in accordance with the contract for the entire validity period of the latest permit. The salary and terms of employment must still correspond to Danish standards.
benefits: No specific educational background is required.
Family members (spouse/partner and children under 18) are eligible to join the applicant.
The spouse/partner of the permit holder is eligible to work in Denmark.
Permit holders are allowed to stay in the Schengen area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
Entitlement to free Danish lessons.
required_documents: Valid passport
Completed application form
Proof of job offer/employment contract meeting salary requirements and Danish standards
Documentation that the job position was advertised on Jobnet and EURES portal for at least 2 weeks
Biometric features (fingerprints and photo)
application_process_steps: Check eligibility requirements and confirm qualification for the visa category.
Gather all required documents, including the job offer and proof of job advertisement.
Submit the application through the official immigration portal or consulate.
Pay the application fee.
Have biometric features recorded (fingerprints and photo) within 14 days of submission.
Attend any required appointments or interviews.

visas.name: Positive List Scheme
visas.description: The Positive List Scheme in Denmark is designed to attract foreign skilled professionals to fill specific occupations experiencing a shortage of qualified workers. It grants a residence and work permit to individuals who have received a job offer for a position listed on one of Denmark's Positive Lists. The scheme facilitates a streamlined immigration process for these in-demand roles.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled professionals from non-EU/EEA countries who possess relevant educational qualifications (at least a 3-year bachelor's degree or vocational training) and have secured a job offer in an occupation listed on the Danish Positive List.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of a Positive List work and residence permit can typically apply for permanent residency after a minimum period of legal residence (often 8 years is cited by third-party sources, but SIRI states 'meeting specific criteria' without a precise timeline on its main pages), demonstrating Danish language proficiency (e.g., B1 level), and an understanding of Danish society and culture. After obtaining permanent residency, a path to citizenship may be available.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to be employed in the same position and by the same employer, with salary and work conditions corresponding to Danish standards. The permit can be extended even if the profession is no longer on the Positive List. Receiving public assistance under the Active Social Policy Act may prevent extension.
benefits: Streamlined application process for work and residence permits.
Addresses skill gaps in critical sectors of the Danish economy.
Provides a clear pathway to employment in Denmark for qualified individuals.
Allows family members to apply for accompanying residence permits.
Offers entitlement to free Danish language lessons.
required_documents: Documentation of paid application fee
Copy of all pages of a valid passport (including empty pages and covers)
Employment contract or job offer detailing salary and employment conditions
Documentation of educational qualifications relevant to the offered job
Documentation of any required Danish authorization for regulated professions
application_process_steps: Secure a job offer from a Danish employer for a position on the Positive List.
Gather all required documentation, including passport, employment contract, and educational credentials.
Complete the application form (AR1 or AR6 if employer has power of attorney) through the official immigration portal (nyidanmark.dk).
Pay the application fee.
Have biometric features recorded within 14 days of submitting the application.
Await decision from the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration (SIRI).

visas.name: Researcher (Paid Position)
visas.description: The 'Researcher (Paid Position)' program in Denmark is a residence and work permit designed for individuals who have been offered a paid employment as a researcher at a Danish research institution or company. The primary purpose of the role must be research, and the salary and employment terms must align with Danish standards.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who have secured a paid researcher position with a Danish research institution or company.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After a period of legal residency (typically 8 years, or 4 years in some cases), researchers can apply for a permanent residence permit. Conditions include being over 18, meeting current permit requirements, no criminal convictions, no overdue public debts, not having received certain social benefits, accepting a declaration of residence and self-support, current employment, passing Danish language test 2, and having been employed full-time for at least 3 years and 6 months within the last 4 years.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the conditions for the residence and work permit, including maintaining a salary and terms of employment that correspond to Danish standards.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Danish resident tax rules apply. No special tax treatment is explicitly mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Ability to live and work legally in Denmark.
Opportunity for spouse and children to join on dependent visas.
Spouse is also permitted to work in Denmark.
Path to applying for permanent residency after a few years.
Freedom to travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
required_documents: Documentation of paid application fee (receipt).
Copy of all pages of a valid passport (including empty pages and covers).
Employment contract or job offer from a Danish research institution or company.
Documentation that the applicant is staying legally in Denmark (if applying from within Denmark).
Documentation for any salary components not directly stated in the employment contract (if relevant).
Documentation of educational background relevant to the offered employment (e.g., degree certificates).
Documentation of authorization if the job requires a Danish authorization.
Updated CV.
Passport photo (as per Danish guidelines).
Completed application form (AR1).
application_process_steps: Create a case order ID and pay the application fee online to SIRI.
Employer completes their part of the application (AR1).
Applicant receives an email link to sign up as a user and complete their part of the application (AR1).
Gather all required supporting documentation.
Submit the completed application (AR1 form) along with all documents.
Record biometric features (facial photo and fingerprints) at a Danish diplomatic mission or SIRI branch office no later than 14 days after submitting the application.

visas.name: Guest Researcher
visas.description: The Danish Guest Researcher program allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who have been invited by a Danish research institution or company to conduct research, without being employed by the Danish entity. It grants a residence and work permit for a temporary research stay in Denmark.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals holding a Master's degree (or equivalent) who are invited to conduct research at a Danish institution as part of their continuing education or career, without receiving a salary from the Danish host.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa is for temporary research stays and does not inherently lead to permanent residency. If a guest researcher finds employment in Denmark, a new application for a different type of residence and work permit based on the new employment is required.
visas.renewal_conditions: Can be renewed if the invitation to do research in Denmark is extended, but the total duration of the permit as a guest researcher cannot exceed 3 years on the same research project. Application for extension must be submitted before the current permit expires.
benefits: Allows a stay of up to 3 years for research purposes in Denmark.
Permits accompanying family members (spouse/partner and children under 18) to join the guest researcher.
Provides a basis for registering with the Central Person Register (CPR) and access to public health insurance for stays over 3 months.
Allows limited sideline examination tasks at other universities without a separate work permit.
Permits stay in the Schengen area for up to 90 days within the last 180 days.
required_documents: Invitation letter from a Danish research institution or company

Documentation of sufficient funds to support oneself for the entire period of stay (DKK 12,770 per month for a single person; DKK 25,540 per month if accompanied by a spouse, DKK 29,742 per month if accompanied by spouse and one or more children - 2025 level)
Proof of having completed an educational program at the level of a Master's degree (or equivalent)
Completed application form (AR1 for initial application, AR3 for extension)
Valid passport (permit cannot be valid longer than 3 months before passport expiry)
application_process_steps: Receive an official invitation from a Danish research institution or company.
Create a case order ID for the application and pay the application fee.
The research institution or company completes their part of the application (e.g., in application form AR1).
Submit the completed application (AR1) to the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration (SIRI).
Provide documentation of sufficient funds, educational background, and other required documents.
Wait for SIRI's processing and decision.

visas.name: Special Individual Qualifications (Athlete or Coach)
visas.description: This program is for individuals who have been offered a job as a professional athlete or coach in a Danish sports club. It grants a residence and work permit, allowing the individual to live and work in Denmark based on their special individual qualifications in sports.
visas.target_applicant: Professional athletes or coaches who have secured an employment offer from a Danish sports club affiliated with the National Olympic Committee and Sports Confederation of Denmark (DIF).
visas.path_to_residency_description: While not explicitly detailed for this specific visa, generally, continuous legal residence in Denmark for a specified period (typically 5-8 years) under a work permit can lead to eligibility for permanent residency, provided other conditions related to language, employment, and integration are met.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicant must continue to be employed in the same position and by the same employer, and must have worked and received salary in accordance with their contract for the entire validity period of the latest permit.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this permit must be able to support themselves and their family and are not allowed to receive benefits under the Active Social Policy Act. Standard Danish tax rules for residents apply, and no special tax exemptions are mentioned for this category.
benefits: Residence and work permit in Denmark.
Entitlement to free Danish lessons (for those over 18 with a registered Danish address).
Ability to apply for sideline employment with an additional permit.
Family members (spouse, registered/cohabiting partner, and children under 18) can apply for accompanying residence permits.
required_documents: Copy of all pages of your passport (including empty pages and front/back covers).
Employment contract or job offer clearly stating all terms of employment, including salary and holiday entitlements.
Documentation of your special individual qualifications (e.g., athletic level, previous contracts).
Advance statement from the relevant specialized association that is a member of the National Olympic Committee and Sports Confederation of Denmark (DIF).
Documentation of paid application fee (receipt).
Documentation of any parts of your salary or benefits not appearing in the employment contract (e.g., paid housing rent, salary paid abroad), if applicable.
application_process_steps: The employer obtains an advance statement from the relevant Danish sports governing body (if required).
The employer completes the first part of the application form (AR1).
The applicant creates a case order ID and pays the application fee online.
The applicant completes their part of the application form.

The application, along with all required documents (employment contract, passport copies, advance statement, fee receipt), is submitted to the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration (SIRI).
The applicant must have their biometric features (facial photo and fingerprints) recorded no later than 14 days after submitting the application.

visas.name: Special Individual Qualifications (Specialised Chef)
visas.description: This visa is for highly qualified chefs who have been offered a job in Denmark at a restaurant with an innovative character and a high gastronomic level. It grants a residence and work permit, allowing the holder to live and work in Denmark for a specific employer and job.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a chef with documented international recognition, significant experience from internationally recognised restaurants, or gastronomic competition wins, who has a job offer from a qualifying Danish restaurant.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The permit can be renewed for increasing periods (1, 2, then 3 years), implying a long-term stay which can lead to permanent residency. General work permit holders may eventually qualify for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be renewed for 1 year at a time during the first 2 years, then for a maximum of 2 years, and after 4 years, for a maximum of 3 years at a time. Validity cannot exceed the length of the job contract. Salary and terms of employment must continue to correspond to Danish standards. The permit is tied to the specific job and employer; a new permit is required for a new job.
benefits: Obtain a residence and work permit in Denmark.
Opportunity to work in innovative and high-level gastronomic restaurants.
Pathway to long-term stay and potential permanent residency.
Family members may be allowed to accompany the applicant.
required_documents: Receipt for paid application fee
Copy of all pages of passport (including empty pages and covers)
Employment contract or job offer (must include salary, terms, job description, and not be more than 30 days old)
Documentation of education relevant to the job offered
Documentation of work experience relevant to the job offered
Documentation of special individual qualifications (e.g., titles from international chef competitions, international recognition)
Documentation of any salary components not directly in contract (e.g., paid rent, salary paid abroad)
Declaration of self-support for applicant and accompanying family members (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Obtain a binding job offer from a Danish restaurant with an innovative character and/or high gastronomic level.
Create a case order ID and pay the application fee to SIRI (Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration).
Gather all required documents, including passport, employment contract, educational and work experience documentation, and proof of special qualifications.
Submit the application, either online or at a Danish embassy/diplomatic mission if applying from abroad, or at SIRI's Citizen Centre or a local police station if already in Denmark.
Record biometrics (fingerprints and ID photo).
Await processing and decision from SIRI.

visas.name: Special Individual Qualifications (Other Qualifications)
visas.description: This visa is for individuals who have been offered a job in Denmark that is uniquely linked to their personal qualifications, meaning no one else can immediately perform the job. It grants a residence and work permit in Denmark.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant has highly specialized or unique skills and has secured a job offer in Denmark that requires these specific individual qualifications.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holding a residence and work permit based on special individual qualifications is a step towards potential permanent residency. General requirements for permanent residency in Denmark typically include a certain period of legal residence, language proficiency, and adherence to various integration requirements, though specific details for this visa category's pathway are not detailed in the provided sources.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to be employed in the same position and by the same employer, have worked and received salary in accordance with the contract for the entire validity period, and salary/terms of employment must continue to correspond to Danish standards. Must not have received public benefits.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Danish tax rules for residents apply. Salary must be paid into a Danish bank account in the applicant's name.
benefits: Ability to live and work in Denmark for a specific employer and role.
Opportunity for family reunification (dependants allowed).
Entitlement to free Danish lessons for adults over 18 with a registered Danish address.
Potential path to permanent residency in Denmark.
required_documents: Receipt for paid application fee
Copy of all pages of your passport (including empty pages and front/back cover)
Employment contract or job offer
Documentation of education relevant to the job offered
Documentation of work experience relevant to the job offered
Documentation of any parts of your salary or benefits not appearing in the employment contract (e.g., paid rent or salary paid abroad)
Any other documentation of your special individual qualifications
application_process_steps: Create a case order ID and pay the application fee to SIRI.
Employer completes the first part of the application (form AR1).
Applicant receives an email and completes their part of the application.
Submit the application along with all required supporting documents.
Have biometric data (fingerprints and facial photo) recorded at a Danish diplomatic mission, application center, or SIRI Citizen Centre.

visas.name: Herdsmen and Farm Managers
visas.description: The Danish Herdsmen and Farm Manager work permit is an employer-sponsored residence and work permit for skilled agricultural professionals seeking salaried employment in Denmark. It is specifically designed for herdsmen (livestock managers) and farm managers (supervisory agricultural roles), and general farm workers, mink farm handlers, and managers in horticulture or forestry are ineligible.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled agricultural professionals, aged 18 or older, with professional qualifications in herdsman or farm manager disciplines, who have secured a job offer in Denmark meeting Danish salary standards.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 4 years of continuous employment, workers can pursue permanent residence, which typically requires meeting additional criteria such as Danish language level 3, an above-average income, and active citizenship demonstration. A pathway to Danish citizenship follows permanent residence status.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be extended if the applicant continues to be employed in the same position and by the same employer. If a new job is found, a new application based on the new job must be submitted.
benefits: Access to Denmark's public healthcare system.
Unrestricted travel within the Schengen area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period (though work outside Denmark is prohibited).
Ability to sponsor family members to join them in Denmark.
Pathway to permanent residence after 4 years of continuous employment, followed by a potential pathway to Danish citizenship.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least 6 months remaining validity (all pages copied).
Employment contract or job offer, dated within 30 days of application, specifying salary, hours, duties, start date, and duration.
Application form (AR1 requiring both employer-applicant or AR6 for employer-authorized power of attorney).
Proof of visa fee payment (receipt of DKK 6,810).
Biometric recording (fingerprints and facial photo) scheduled within 14 days of application submission.
Documentation of professional qualifications relevant to the offered job (diploma or certification from a relevant educational program in herdsman or farm manager disciplines).
Documentation of parts of salary or benefits not explicitly in the employment contract (e.g., paid rent for housing), if applicable.
Documentation of legal stay in Denmark, if applicable.
application_process_steps: Create a case order ID on SIRI's official portal.
Pay the application fee and retain the payment receipt.
Complete and submit the digital application form (AR1 or AR6), with the employer completing their part.
Attach all required digital documents (passport, employment contract, proof of qualifications).
Schedule and complete biometric recording (fingerprints and facial photo) within 14 days of application submission.
Wait for a response from SIRI (normal processing time is 1 month).

visas.name: Student Residence Permit (Higher Education)
visas.description: The Student Residence Permit (Higher Education) in Denmark is for non-EU/EEA citizens admitted to a full-time higher educational program in Denmark. It allows individuals to live and study in Denmark for the duration of their academic program.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA citizens who have been admitted to a state-approved, full-time higher educational program (Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, or preparatory courses for higher education) at a Danish institution.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Upon completion of a state-approved higher educational program, students can apply for an 'Establishment Card' (job-seeking permit) allowing them to stay and work in Denmark for up to three years to seek employment.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to be enrolled in the same study program and participate actively. Must demonstrate sufficient funds (DKK 7,426 per month for the extended period, capped at 12 months). Extensions beyond 1 year are typically only granted due to serious illness or if the initial permit was shortened by passport expiry. Applications must be submitted no earlier than 4 months before expiry.
visas.tax_implications: Students are generally subject to limited tax liability on Danish-earned income (e.g., salary, student grants) for the first 365 days of stay within a 2-year period. Full tax liability, including on non-Danish income, commences from day 366. Double taxation treaties may apply. Students should contact SKAT (Danish tax authority) upon arrival or if working.
benefits: Right to reside and study in Denmark for the duration of the permit's validity.
Ability to work part-time (90 hours per month from September to June, full-time in June, July, and August).
Path to an 'Establishment Card' (job-seeking permit) for up to 3 years after graduation.
Access to public healthcare system after obtaining a CPR number and yellow health card.
Opportunity for family members (spouse, registered partner, cohabiting partner, and children under 18) to join with separate permits.
required_documents: Documentation of paid case processing fee to SIRI (receipt or bank statement)
Copy of all pages of a valid passport (including empty pages and covers)
Letter of acceptance/documentation of enrolment from a Danish educational institution (full-time program)
Documentation showing ability to support oneself financially (bank statement less than 30 days old, in applicant's name, or proof of paid tuition fee for the first semester/year)
Passport photo meeting biometric standards
Completed application form (ST1, often filled in collaboration with the university)
application_process_steps: Be admitted to a higher educational program at a Danish institution.
Create a case order ID online via SIRI's portal.
Pay the application fee to SIRI (DKK 3,060 for 2026).
Gather all required supporting documents.
Complete the application form (ST1), often with assistance from the Danish university.
Submit the application online or at the nearest Danish Embassy/General Consulate/VFS-station and have biometric features recorded within 14 days of submission.

visas.name: Family Reunification (Spouse/Partner)
visas.description: This visa allows a foreign national spouse or partner to reunite and live long-term with their spouse or cohabiting partner who is a Danish citizen or holds a legal residence permit (other than asylum) in Denmark. The residence permit is initially temporary but can be extended and eventually lead to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: A person who is legally married, in a registered partnership, or is a long-term cohabiting partner of an individual residing legally in Denmark.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A temporary residence permit can lead to permanent residency after 8 years of lawful residence. This period can be reduced to 4 years if specific supplementary conditions are met, such as being in full-time employment for at least 3 years and 6 months within the preceding 4 years, meeting income thresholds (e.g., annual average income above DKK 346,155.57 for the last 2 years for the sponsor in certain cases), and passing an active citizen exam or demonstrating active citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the original residence permit conditions. The sponsor may need to extend a collateral guarantee for a total period of 10 years from the initial guarantee's start date.
benefits: Ability to live legally with spouse/partner in Denmark long-term.
Normally grants the right to work in Denmark.
Provides a path to permanent residency in Denmark.
Allows for extension of the initial temporary residence permit.
required_documents: Application Form 1 (for the applicant) and Form 2 (for the spouse/partner in Denmark)
Copy of passport (all pages, including cover) for the applicant
Legally valid marriage certificate (with authorized translation to Danish or English) or documentation of cohabitation for at least 18 months if unmarried
Statement from the Danish municipality (kommune) confirming no receipt of public assistance by the sponsor
Documentation of the sponsor's housing situation (must be of reasonable size and not in a restricted area)
Pledge of financial support for the applicant signed by the sponsor
Documentation of cohabitation (e.g., rental agreement, letters received at same address, statements from landlords/employers - if not married/registered partners)
Proof of previous visit to Denmark by the applicant
Documentation related to meeting integration requirements (for both applicant and sponsor)
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility and gather all necessary documents according to the checklist (Forms 1 and 2, passport copies, marriage/cohabitation proof, etc.).
Create a case order ID and pay the application fee (DKK 8,490 to the Danish Immigration Service and potentially DKK 1,875 embassy fee if applying from abroad).

Submit the completed application form(s) and all required documentation to a Danish diplomatic mission abroad or, if the applicant is legally in Denmark, to the Danish Immigration Service's Citizen Service or local police.
Provide biometric data (photograph and fingerprints) at the designated location.
Await a decision from the Danish Immigration Service (expected maximum processing time is 10 months).
If approved, receive a temporary residence permit allowing residence and work in Denmark.

visas.name: Family Reunification (Children)
visas.description: This program allows children to obtain a residence permit in Denmark to live with a parent who is a Danish citizen, a citizen of another Nordic country, holds a permanent residence permit, or has refugee status in Denmark. The aim is to reunite immediate family members, ensuring the child's best interests are met.
visas.target_applicant: Children under 15 years old are generally the primary applicants, though children between 15 and 18 years old may qualify under very special circumstances, provided they have a parent legally residing in Denmark.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The initial residence permit is temporary. It can be extended, and after living in Denmark for a certain period under family reunification, the individual can apply for a permanent residence permit, provided all conditions continue to be met.
visas.renewal_conditions: The residence permit is initially temporary, typically valid until the child turns 18 years old. It can be extended if the child and the parent continue to meet the original requirements. After turning 18, extensions are typically granted for 4 years at a time. The parent in Denmark must not have been found guilty by a Danish court of child abuse within the past 10 years. The child must live at the same address as the parent in Denmark, and family reunification must be in the child's best interest. The child may not have started their own family.
benefits: Allows the child to live with their parent in Denmark.
The residence permit normally grants the right to work in Denmark (applicable to older children).
Provides a pathway to apply for permanent residency in Denmark after a certain period.
Ensures family unity and the child's well-being in Denmark.
required_documents: Application fee payment documentation
Copy of all pages of the child's passport (including empty pages and covers)
Child's Certificate of Personal Data (Birth Certificate) with an authorised translation to Danish or English
Documentation of custody (if applicable, with authorised translation)
One passport photo (if a residence card is not desired immediately, otherwise biometric data is taken)
Forms FA6 and FA7 (application packet for children)
application_process_steps: Go to newtodenmark.dk and navigate to the family reunification section for children.
Create a case order ID and pay the application fee.
Fill out the relevant application form (FA6 or FA7 for children).
Gather and attach all required supporting documents.
Submit the application and documents, either electronically or in person at a Danish Immigration Service location or relevant representation abroad.

visas.name: Religious Worker
visas.description: This visa is for foreign nationals seeking a residence and work permit in Denmark to serve as a member of the clergy, a missionary, or to perform other religious functions within an officially acknowledged or sanctioned religious order or denomination. It allows individuals to reside and work in Denmark while fulfilling their religious duties.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a member of the clergy, a missionary, a nun, or a monk who can document affiliation with an officially acknowledged or sanctioned religious denomination in Denmark and has relevant background, training, or education.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must complete a course about Danish family law, individual rights, and democracy within six months of being granted the initial residence permit. The permit can be extended for one year at a time, for a maximum of three years in total, or without an upper time limit for those authorized to perform weddings.
benefits: Allows residence in Denmark
Grants a work permit to engage in religious work
Family members can apply as accompanying dependants
Possibility of extension for up to three years, or indefinitely for those authorized to perform weddings
Provides a legal framework for religious service in Denmark
required_documents: Documentation for payment of fee
Copy of passport (all pages including front page)
Documentation for relevant background, training and/or education
Written agreement or declaration from the Danish denomination stating the applicant's role
Sworn declaration regarding not engaging in activities that threaten public safety, law and order, health, decency, or rights/duties of others
Declaration stating no public assistance will be received by the applicant or accompanying family members
Declaration stating adherence to Danish laws including freedom of expression, freedom of religion, gender equality, sexual orientation, non-discrimination, and women's rights
Documentation for completion of a course about Danish family law, individual rights and democracy (for extensions only)
application_process_steps: The religious order/denomination in Denmark completes Part 1 of the RF1 online form (sections 10-12) and signs it using NemID/MitID.
The religious order/denomination attaches required documentation and forwards the completed form to the applicant.
The applicant (religious worker) completes Part 2 of the RF1 online form (sections 1-7) and signs it.
The applicant attaches their required documentation, including proof of fee payment and passport copies.

The applicant submits the complete application (both parts and all documents) at a Danish diplomatic mission in their country of residence or, if legally residing in Denmark, at the Danish Immigration Service's Citizen Service (by appointment), or by mail.
The Danish Immigration Service processes the application.

visas.name: Au Pair Scheme
visas.description: The Danish Au Pair Scheme is a cultural exchange program allowing young foreign nationals to live with a Danish host family and experience Danish language and culture. In return for food, accommodation, and pocket money, the au pair participates in daily domestic chores and childcare.
visas.target_applicant: Young, unmarried individuals without children, aged 18-29, who wish to improve their language and cultural skills by living with a Danish host family.
visas.renewal_conditions: Can be renewed up to a total maximum stay of 24 months, provided the au pair remains with the same host family and the conditions for the stay remain unchanged. The permit cannot exceed the duration of the contract or the point at which the youngest child in the family turns 18.
visas.tax_implications: Au pairs must pay tax on their monthly pocket money. It is mandatory to apply for a tax card at the local tax centre after receiving a CPR number and opening a Danish bank account.
benefits: Free accommodation and full board with a host family.
Monthly pocket money (stipend).
Entitlement to free Danish language lessons.
Host family provides accident and injury insurance, and covers repatriation in serious cases.
Access to free healthcare through the Danish system after registration as a resident.
required_documents: Valid passport or national ID card
Signed Au Pair contract between au pair and host family
Proof of payment for the application fee
Proof of language skills in Danish, Swedish, Norwegian, English, or German (moderate level)
Copies of school certificates or other proof of education (equivalent to nine years of schooling)
Copy of birth certificate
Biometric data (photo and fingerprints)
Additional documents may be required based on nationality and case
application_process_steps: Find a suitable Danish host family and agree on an au pair contract.
Host family completes their part of the online application and receives a pre-filled contract via Digital Post for signature.
Au pair signs the contract and gathers all required supporting documents.
Create a case order ID and pay the application fee of DKK 4,305.
Submit the application (online or paper form) to SIRI or a Danish diplomatic mission.
Submit biometric features (photo and fingerprints) within 14 days of application submission.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: A child born on or after July 1, 2014, automatically acquires Danish citizenship if the mother, father, or co-mother is a Danish citizen, regardless of birthplace or parental marital status. For children born before this date, rules vary based on the law at the time of birth; typically, citizenship passed through the father if parents were married, or the mother if unmarried. Direct descent from a Danish parent is required; having a Danish grandparent is not sufficient. Special exceptions, such as 'The Princess Rule,' apply to certain individuals born between January 1, 1961, and December 31, 1978, to Danish mothers and foreign fathers.

Naturalization.desc: Generally requires continuous legal residence in Denmark for 9 years. This period is reduced for certain groups: Nordic citizens (2 years), refugees and stateless persons (8 years), and individuals who received substantial education in Denmark (5 years). Applicants must hold a permanent residence permit for at least 2 years (1 year for refugees/stateless persons), declare allegiance and loyalty to Denmark, pass Danish language and citizenship tests, demonstrate self-sufficiency (no significant public benefits), and have no serious criminal record or public debt.

Birthright.desc: Denmark does not grant automatic citizenship solely based on birth within its territory (Jus soli). The primary determining factor for automatic citizenship at birth is parentage. A foundling found in the Realm is, until otherwise stated, deemed to have Danish citizenship.

Spouse and Family.desc: Spouses of Danish citizens may apply for naturalization with a reduced continuous residence requirement of 6 to 8 years, depending on the length of the marriage, provided the Danish spouse has been a citizen for at least 3 years. However, a permanent residence permit, which typically requires 8 years of residence, is a prerequisite for citizenship. The '24-year rule' applies to family reunification for married couples, requiring both spouses to be at least 24 years old and the couple's ties to Denmark to be stronger than to the country of origin. The Danish spouse must also meet financial support requirements. If parents marry after a child's birth, the child acquires Danish citizenship if unmarried and under 18 at the time of marriage.

tax_advice:
- **Corporate Tax:** The corporate tax rate in Denmark is 22% for 2024 and 2025, applied to net corporate income.
- **Personal Income Tax:** Residents are taxed on their worldwide income. The marginal tax rate, including labor market tax, can be up to approximately 57% (60.5% including labor market tax for DTT purposes) in 2026, though effective rates are often lower due to deductions. Local tax rates vary, averaging about 25.18% in 2024, excluding church tax. State tax includes a basic rate of 12.091% and a high rate of 15% for income exceeding DKK 640,109 (2024) after labor market contributions.
- **Special Expat Tax Scheme:** Highly qualified foreign professionals and researchers can opt for a flat tax rate of 27% on their gross salary (total 32.84% including an 8% labor market contribution) for up to 84 months (7 years). Conditions apply, including a minimum average monthly salary of DKK 78,000 in 2025, decreasing to DKK 65,400 in 2026.
- **VAT (Value Added Tax):** Denmark applies a single, flat VAT rate of 25% to most goods and services, with no reduced rates. A 0% rate applies to specific items like newspapers, journals, and international transport.
- **Share Income Tax:** Net share income up to DKK 67,500 (2025) is taxed at 27%, with exceeding amounts taxed at 42%.
- **Inheritance Tax:** Inheritance from a Danish resident is subject to a flat rate of 15% on values exceeding DKK 346,000 (2025), with an additional 25% for non-closely related recipients.
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** Denmark has a high cost of living, particularly in major cities like Copenhagen, so meticulous budgeting is essential.
- **Language:** While Danes are generally proficient in English, learning Danish is crucial for deeper integration into society. Free Danish classes are often available for expats for up to 5 years.
- **Safety:** Denmark is one of the safest countries in the world, with very low crime rates. Petty theft can occur in crowded tourist areas, so remain vigilant.
- **Registration:** Non-EU/EEA citizens typically need a residence permit before arrival. Upon arrival, register your address with the local municipality or an International Citizen Service center within five days to obtain a CPR (Civil Registration) number. The CPR number is vital for accessing healthcare, opening bank accounts, and other public services.
- **Transportation:** Public transportation is efficient, and cycling is a popular and cost-effective mode of transport in urban areas. Car ownership is less common due to high taxes and fuel costs.
